The '''Hubble time-scale''', denoted by $t_H$, is a measurement of the '''characteristic time-scale''' of '''[[cosmic expansion]]'''.

It is defined:

$$
t_H(t) \equiv H^{-1}(t) \equiv ( \left(\frac{\dot{a}(t)}{a(t)}\right)^{-1}).
$$

where $H\equiv\dot{a}/a$ is the [[Hubble parameter]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Significance ==

=== $t_\Gamma \ll t_H \Rightarrow $ Efficient reaction ===

A physical process with rate $\Gamma$ remains efficient while

$$
\Gamma\gg H,
$$

and freezes out when

$$
\Gamma\sim H \Rightarrow t_{\text{reaction}}\sim t_H.
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
